briefs.title: SaaS landing page
briefs.text: Tempo is a shared calendar tool for small teams of 5 to 50 people. Its main selling point is "automatically finds a time when everyone is free." Build a marketing landing page: a hero with a headline and a primary button, three core features, a testimonials section (using names that are obviously placeholders), a three-tier pricing table (Free / $9 / $19 per person per month), and a footer.

briefs.title: Analytics dashboard
briefs.text: An operations dashboard for the owner of a coffee chain with 4 locations. Show three metric cards: today's revenue, number of orders, and average order value; a line chart of revenue over the last 30 days; a bar chart comparing sales across locations; a table of the top 5 best-selling items; and a date range picker. Use hard-coded sample data.

briefs.title: Mobile app
briefs.text: The "My Plants" home screen of a plant care app, designed for a phone screen. At the top, a greeting and how many plants need watering today; a list of plant cards, each with the plant's name, species, next watering time, and a "Watered" button; a bottom navigation bar with 4 tabs; and an "Add plant" floating action button in the bottom-right corner.

briefs.title: Sign-up form
briefs.text: A registration page for an online coding summer camp. On the left, an introduction to the camp and three highlights; on the right, a registration form: parent's name, email, child's grade (dropdown), areas of interest (multiple choice: games, robotics, web), session dates (single choice from three sessions), and a submit button. Include form validation messages and a success state after submitting.

briefs.title: SkillArena itself
briefs.text: SkillArena is a website that compares UI skills for AI coding agents. Build its home page: a header with the logo and navigation (Matrix, Compare, About, Waitlist); a hero that explains that every page on the site was generated from the same product brief with a different skill; a matrix where rows are skills (the first row is a "no skill" control group) and columns are four briefs, each cell showing a screenshot thumbnail (use placeholder boxes); and a waitlist form with email and a role choice. Use placeholder skill names.
